name: UI

require.label: route the design to the project

blurb: Screens and flows from the features — the user designs them in Claude Design and provides the files.
prompt:
With the features defined, generate a **Claude Design kickoff** the user can paste straight into
a Claude Design session — built FROM the existing planned features. Read the features and write, at
`prompts/ui-kickoff.md`, a self-contained brief: the product goal; the **feature → screen map**
(which screens each feature needs); for each screen its purpose, key states, and primary flows; and
the design-system constraints (tokens, components, layout). Make it concrete enough that Claude
Design can produce the screens without re-asking. Also write `ui.md` with the screen inventory the
Render preview can visualize.

**Do NOT design the screens yourself** — the visual design comes from the user via Claude Design.
Once the kickoff is written, tell the user to take it to Claude Design, design the screens there,
and bring the exported `.dc.html` design files back by dropping them into the UI panel — that routes
the design to the project and clears this stage.

Gate: the Claude Design files are provided and the design is routed to the project.
